title: Mango Fonio Salad
localName: Salade de fonio à la mangue
author: Pierre Thiam
desc: Cooked fonio with mango, cucumber, grape tomatoes, red onion, parsley and mint, in a vinaigrette of two lemons and a full cup of olive oil.
longDesc: The WBUR printing of a salad from Thiam’s book ‘Senegal’. A vinaigrette of the juice of two lemons, salt and pepper is whisked while a cup of olive oil is added slowly to emulsify. Two cups of cooked fonio (or quinoa) are combined with chopped parsley and mint, diced mango, red onion, halved grape tomatoes and diced cucumber; vinaigrette is added to taste and the salad is topped with spiced cashews if you have them. The page notes some vinaigrette may be left over.
ingredients: 1 cup red and yellow grape tomatoes, halved
1/2 cup spiced cashews (optional; the sub-recipe is not printed)
steps: Whisk the lemon juice, salt and pepper. Slowly whisk in the oil to emulsify.
In a large bowl combine the fonio, parsley, mint, mango, red onion, tomatoes and cucumber.
Toss, adding vinaigrette to taste. Top with cashews if using and serve immediately.
chefTips: The oil-to-lemon ratio (1 cup to the juice of 2 lemons) is the page’s; some vinaigrette will be left over.
Add the dressing to taste rather than all at once.
Cook the fonio ahead and let it cool.
Quinoa substitutes if you cannot find fonio.
commonMistakes: Dressing the salad too early so the mango softens.
Pouring the oil in too fast.
reheating: Serve cold or at room temperature.
healthBenefits: Mango and tomato give vitamin C and carotenoids.
culturalNote: Compare the Yolélé company’s ‘Fonio Mango Salad’: 1/3 cup olive oil against this cup, one lemon against two, grated ginger, 4 cups of fonio against 2, six servings against four. It is a related but distinct formula and carries no book credit; it is not entered here.
sources: Source: WBUR ‘Here & Now’, ‘Senegalese Recipes From Chef Pierre Thiam’, 19 October 2015; no article byline; recipes from ‘Senegal’ (Lake Isle Press), reprinted with permission. Yield: ‘Serves 4’ (two-pass). Quantities SINGLE-PASS. NO TIMES and NO DONENESS CUES anywhere — absent.
The only technique cue is ‘to emulsify’.
